absent: No locking, concurrency, ordering or lifetime rules appear in these fragments.
No function bodies, call sequences or state-machine transitions appear in these fragments.
No wire byte order, alignment, padding or serialization rules appear beyond member order and fixed sizes.
No numeric values for HZ, PATH_MAX, NAME_MAX, sockaddr_in layout or fixed-width integer widths appear in these fragments.
No ioctl return semantics, privilege checks, error mapping or capability requirements appear in these fragments.
No mount parsing, negotiation, fallback or version-selection behavior appears in these fragments.

findings.text: These user-visible headers publish wire, mount and namespace contracts without implementation logic. They define result codes, file kinds, size caps, procedure numbers, mount arguments, flush and debug switches, access-control numbers and namespace queries for use by user space and mount helpers.

Shared result codes use small integers for long-standing failures. NFS_OK is zero; NFSERR_PERM is one; NFSERR_NOENT is two; NFSERR_IO is five; NFSERR_NXIO is six; NFSERR_ACCES is thirteen; NFSERR_EXIST is seventeen; NFSERR_XDEV is eighteen; NFSERR_NODEV is nineteen; NFSERR_NOTDIR is twenty; NFSERR_ISDIR is twenty-one; NFSERR_INVAL is twenty-two; NFSERR_FBIG is twenty-seven; NFSERR_NOSPC is twenty-eight; NFSERR_ROFS is thirty; NFSERR_MLINK is thirty-one; NFSERR_NAMETOOLONG is sixty-three; NFSERR_NOTEMPTY is sixty-six; NFSERR_DQUOT is sixty-nine; NFSERR_STALE is seventy; NFSERR_REMOTE is seventy-one; NFSERR_WFLUSH is ninety-nine. Annotations tie each to generations two, three or four.

Extended codes near ten thousand cover handle, cookie and operation faults. NFSERR_BADHANDLE is 10001; NFSERR_NOT_SYNC is 10002; NFSERR_BAD_COOKIE is 10003; NFSERR_NOTSUPP is 10004; NFSERR_TOOSMALL is 10005; NFSERR_SERVERFAULT is 10006; NFSERR_BADTYPE is 10007; NFSERR_JUKEBOX is 10008; NFSERR_SAME is 10009; NFSERR_DENIED is 10010; NFSERR_EXPIRED is 10011; NFSERR_LOCKED is 10012; NFSERR_GRACE is 10013; NFSERR_FHEXPIRED is 10014; NFSERR_SHARE_DENIED is 10015; NFSERR_WRONGSEC is 10016; NFSERR_CLID_INUSE is 10017; NFSERR_RESOURCE is 10018; NFSERR_MOVED is 10019; NFSERR_NOFILEHANDLE is 10020; NFSERR_MINOR_VERS_MISMATCH is 10021; NFSERR_STALE_CLIENTID is 10022; NFSERR_STALE_STATEID is 10023; NFSERR_OLD_STATEID is 10024; NFSERR_BAD_STATEID is 10025; NFSERR_BAD_SEQID is 10026; NFSERR_NOT_SAME is 10027; NFSERR_LOCK_RANGE is 10028.

Remaining generation-four codes run contiguously to the end of the table. NFSERR_SYMLINK is 10029; NFSERR_RESTOREFH is 10030; NFSERR_LEASE_MOVED is 10031; NFSERR_ATTRNOTSUPP is 10032; NFSERR_NO_GRACE is 10033; NFSERR_RECLAIM_BAD is 10034; NFSERR_RECLAIM_CONFLICT is 10035; NFSERR_BAD_XDR is 10036; NFSERR_LOCKS_HELD is 10037; NFSERR_OPENMODE is 10038; NFSERR_BADOWNER is 10039; NFSERR_BADCHAR is 10040; NFSERR_BADNAME is 10041; NFSERR_BAD_RANGE is 10042; NFSERR_LOCK_NOTSUPP is 10043; NFSERR_OP_ILLEGAL is 10044; NFSERR_DEADLOCK is 10045; NFSERR_FILE_OPEN is 10046; NFSERR_ADMIN_REVOKED is 10047; NFSERR_CB_PATH_DOWN is 10048.

File-kind vocabularies use nine values with one reordering. Common names map non-file to zero, regular to one, directory to two, block to three, character to four, link to five, socket to six, bad to seven and fifo to eight. Generation-two names with NF2 prefix repeat those numbers. Generation-three names with NF3 prefix keep zero through six but assign fifo to seven and bad to eight, swapping the last two.

Generation-two boundaries fix service port at 2049, largest payload at 8192, longest path at 1024, longest name at 255, most groups at 16, handle store at 32, cookie store at 4 and fifo-device sentinel at negative one.
Generation-two mode encoding reserves octal 0170000 as format mask with directory 0040000, character 0020000, block 0060000, regular 0100000, link 0120000, socket 0140000 and fifo 0010000.

Generation-two program version is two. Procedure identifiers run null zero, getattr one, setattr two, root three, lookup four, readlink five, read six, writecache seven, write eight, create nine, remove ten, rename eleven, link twelve, symlink thirteen, mkdir fourteen, rmdir fifteen, readdir sixteen and statfs seventeen.
Generation-two handle is a fixed opaque byte array sized by the generation-two handle length, with no length member or variant layout described.

Generation-three keeps port 2049, group cap 16, cookie size 4 and fifo sentinel negative one, widens payload to 32768 and handle to 64, adds three eight-byte verifier sizes for create, cookie and write, derives path cap from PATH_MAX and name cap from NAME_MAX, and repeats the generation-two octal mode mask and type bits identically.

Access bits are read 0x0001, lookup 0x0002, modify 0x0004, extend 0x0008, delete 0x0010, execute 0x0020 and full 0x003f. Creation modes are unchecked zero, guarded one and exclusive two. Capability flags are link 0x0001, symlink 0x0002, homogeneous 0x0008 and cansettime 0x0010, with combined default 0x001B, billyboy 0x0018 and readonly 0x0008.

Generation-three time handling offers dont-change zero, server-time one and client-time two. Program version is three and mount companion version is three. Procedures run null zero, getattr one, setattr two, lookup three, access four, readlink five, read six, write seven, create eight, mkdir nine, symlink ten, mknod eleven, remove twelve, rmdir thirteen, rename fourteen, link fifteen, readdir sixteen, readdirplus seventeen, fsstat eighteen, fsinfo nineteen, pathconf twenty and commit twenty-one.
Generation-three handle pairs a short length with a fixed store sized by the generation-three handle length, so transmitted length varies up to the maximum while backing storage stays constant.

Sizes are bitmap three, sequence four, other twelve, total sixteen, opaque 1024, session sixteen, path from PATH_MAX and name from NAME_MAX. Access is read 0x0001, lookup 0x0002, modify 0x0004, extend 0x0008, delete 0x0010, execute 0x0020, xaread 0x0040, xawrite 0x0080 and xalist 0x0100. Handle flags are persistent zero, noexpire-with-open one, volatile-any two, migration four and rename eight. Open results are confirm 0x0002, posix-lock 0x0004, preserve-unlinked 0x0008, no-stateid 0x0010 and may-notify 0x0020. Share mask is 0x000F with access read one write two both three and deny read one write two both three.

Delegation desires pack type in a high byte under mask 0xFF00 with none zero, read 0x0100, write 0x0200, any 0x0300, no-deleg 0x0400 and cancel 0x0500. Timing uses mask 0xF0000 with resource-available 0x10000 and uncontended-push 0x20000. Modifiers use mask 0xF00000 with timestamps 0x100000 and xor 0x200000, with a combined want mask covering type plus modifiers. Coordination values are fore one, back two and both three, with one family also defining fore-or-both three and back-or-both seven. Time selectors are server zero and client one. Entry kinds are allow zero, deny one, audit two and alarm three. Support bits are allow one, deny two, audit four and alarm eight. List flags are auto-inherit one, protected two and defaulted four.

Inheritance and audit control use file-inherit 0x01, directory-inherit 0x02, no-propagate 0x04, inherit-only 0x08, success 0x10, failed 0x20, group 0x40 and inherited 0x80. Data rights reuse paired aliases on shared bits with read-list 0x01, write-add-file 0x02, append-add-subdir 0x04, read-named 0x08, write-named 0x10, execute 0x20, delete-child 0x40, read-attrs 0x80, write-attrs 0x100, retention 0x200, retention-hold 0x400, delete 0x10000, read-acl 0x20000, write-acl 0x40000, write-owner 0x80000 and synchronize 0x100000. Rolled-up masks are generic-read 0x120081, generic-write 0x160106, generic-execute 0x1200A0 and all 0x1F01FF.

Exchange-identity capabilities are moved-refer 0x01, moved-migr 0x02, fence-ops 0x04, bind-principal 0x100, non-pnfs 0x10000, mds 0x20000 and ds 0x40000 with pnfs mask 0x70000, update-confirmed 0x40000000 and confirmed 0x80000000, rolled into argument mask 0x40070103, result mask 0x80070103 and extended result mask 0x80070107. Sequence status is path-down 0x01, credentials-expiring 0x02, credentials-expired 0x04, all-revoked 0x08, some-revoked 0x10, admin-revoked 0x20, recallable-revoked 0x40, lease-moved 0x80, reclaim-needed 0x100, session-path-down 0x200 and backchannel-fault 0x400. Security styles are current zero and parent one. The largest 64-bit value is all-bits-set. Compound caps are eight forward and two backchannel operations.

Client defaults set UDP timeout eleven with three retransmits, TCP timeout six hundred with two retransmits, UDP ceiling sixty times HZ and TCP ceiling six hundred times HZ. Attribute-cache windows default to three through sixty for regular files and thirty through sixty for directories.

Flush hints are sync one, stable four, low-priority eight, high-priority sixteen and conditional-stable thirty-two for single-RPC stable writes. Diagnostics are VFS 0x01, dircache 0x02, lookupcache 0x04, pagecache 0x08, proc 0x10, xdr 0x20, file 0x40, root 0x80, callback 0x100, client 0x200, mount 0x400, fscache 0x800, pnfs 0x1000, pnfs-ld 0x2000, state 0x4000, xattrcache 0x8000 and all 0xFFFF.

Mount arguments form a versioned record ordered as version, descriptor, old generation-two root handle, flags, read size, write size, timeout, retransmits, four cache bounds, socket address, hostname sized by max name plus terminator, name length, block size, generation-three root handle, pseudo flavor and context sized by max context plus terminator. Annotations tag each member with its introducing version from one through six while preserving earlier offsets.

Mount program version is six with context cap 256. Option bits are soft 0x01, intr 0x02 retained for compatibility, secure 0x04, posix 0x08, nocto 0x10, noac 0x20, tcp 0x40, ver3 0x80, kerberos 0x100, nonlm 0x200, broken-suid 0x400, noacl 0x800, strictlock 0x1000, secflavour 0x2000, nordirplus 0x4000 and unshared 0x8000, with mask 0xFFFF covering all defined bits.

Access-control side protocol uses program number 100227. Generation-two operations are null zero, getacl one, setacl two, getattr three and access four; generation-three keeps null zero, getacl one and setacl two. Presence bits are acl one, count two, default four and default-count eight with combined mask fifteen, plus a separate default selector 0x1000.

Namespace descriptors expose queries under magic 0xb7. Numbers one through four return owning user namespace, parent, type and owner identifier with no-data encoding. Numbers six through nine translate process identifiers between caller scope and target scope, distinguishing thread versus group breadth and from-versus-in direction, with integer payloads in read encoding. Numbers ten through twelve fetch mount-namespace info for current, next and previous entries using the mount-info record.

Mount-namespace description carries its own byte length, a mount count and a 64-bit identifier in that order with 32-bit, 32-bit then 64-bit widths. First published size is sixteen, so callers size buffers from the leading field and later extensions preserve this prefix.

Stability rules include shared port 2049 across generations, doubled handle storage from generation two to three, delegation of path and name caps to system limits, swapped fifo and bad numbers in generation three, state-identifier total equal to the sum of its parts, mount-record growth only by appending version-tagged members, flag masks exactly covering defined bits, and a published mount-info size smaller than native padded size on 64-bit targets.

Implementers must not assume continuity across status ranges, must treat negative-one fifo device as a sentinel, must scale timeout ceilings by HZ, must honor volatile and migration handle lifetimes, must not assume a request numbered five exists in the namespace series, and must use the leading size field rather than native structure size when exchanging mount-namespace info across word sizes.
